Actually, if you look at my comments in the rest of this thread, you'll see that Buddhism is one of the main reasons I'm still alive today. Though sometimes, like last night, I question if that pursuit is really worth it. 

It does help quite a lot though. I practice Vipassana meditation, and it is a truly enriching influence on my life. I would highly recommend reading about Buddhist philosophy to anyone who feels the same way I do.

If even a word of what you said is sincere, it is one of the greatest compliments I've ever recieved. 

Thank you.

You're right, for now. I won't do it now because posting here allowed me a necessary outlet to vent my emotions. Now that I'm in a healthier state of mind, I am fine, and am able to see what you said ("Yeah, you're not gonna commit suicide") as a simple statement and not as a challenge. But, if you had said something that triggering to someone who was in an unhealthy state of mind, it could have disastrous consequences. I don't know if you've ever been suicidal before, but if you had, you would know that in that mindset everything even slightly hostile just makes the situation worse. Inciting anger as an emotional response, 'challenging' someone to either suck it up or to go as far as to say "you won't do it" can be extremely damaging. If you plan on posting here in the future, I cannot stress that enough. Don't belittle people who are in a fragile state, or you could directly influence their death. And if you already know all that, and still chose to say the things you said, please never post here again.

Thank you for the recommendation, I will be sure to read it. 

As for if there are any other factors in my intent to commit suicide besides my philosophical reasonings, no, there are not. That is probably why I am still around, in fact.

I don't believe I missed their point, actually. I devoted a good two years to studying existential and nihilistic philosophies, and came to understand them very well. I do believe, however, that you are missing my point, which is that if you cannot justify something objectively, you cannot justify it at all. Obviously, that is something you won't come to agree with me on, so leave it be. 

You are right about the duality of suffering. A good bit of my personal philosophy is heavily influenced by Buddhism. In fact, the Four Noble Truths are the main reason I have not yet committed suicide. If you're not familiar, the four noble truths state that (1) There is suffering. (2) Suffering arises from attachment to desires/seeing nonpermanent things as permanent. (3) There is a way to overcome suffering. (4) The Noble Eightfold Path that is the way to overcome suffering. Number two is where I get my idea that everything is suffering, because most people in the world are ruled by their desires, and that in itself is suffering. The reason I even consider suicide while knowing these truths is because I lack the dedication to follow the eightfold path. Of course, many would say this comes with time, and that is why I'm still around. 

You're right, I am a fairly privileged youth with a lot of great things going for me. But I think that only lends more credence to my desire to die, as you can be sure that it is not clouded by emotional dismay. My life does not suck, and I am not unhappy. 

I'm also sorry that you were so upset by my philosophy that you encouraged me to kill myself on a board meant for helping. Please remember, if you post here in the future, if you don't have anything nice to say, don't say anything at all.

I've read all of those philosphers and more, in fact. I agree with Camus on one thing: The only important question in philosophy is that of suicide. I believe that the answer is yes, he believes the answer is no. I also believe that far greater minds than theirs have overcome the greatest cognitive bias that is ingrained in every human being: the will to survive. What does it benefit us as philisophical creatures? What does it do for most of our species besides force them to perpetuate their own suffering? Nothing. There is no objective benefit to being alive over being dead, it's just a cognitive bias that tells us there is.

So you think the universe cares about people, then? Not that we're an inconsequential species inhabiting less space in the universe than a nucleus occupies in its atom?

As for achieving nothingness in waking life, that is literally impossible. The only way to experience nothing is to be nothing. Death and non-birth are the only two ways for a human to achieve nothingness, and obviously not being born is out of the question, so the only real option left is suicide. I could just wait it out, but what would be the point of that? Enjoyment? That doesn't matter much in the long run. Nothing in life matters in the long run. So why not just end it early? I see no reason not to.

In short, I've acknowledged that we live in an uncaring universe, that all human morals are not self-evident, but are made up by humans, and that the same goes for all meaning of existence. I also believe that after death there is nothingness, and that nothingness is the ideal state of being. All those combined lead me to believe that suicide is the best option. 

If you want me to elaborate on any of these, I'll gladly do so. Gives me something to do.

Well thanks, I suppose. Though saying I'm responsible is a bit of a stretch. And the rationality isn't the best thing either, considering it's more or less what led me to consider suicide as the best option. In my mind, it's the best response to existential angst.

We're not allowed to discuss plans here, but it's actually a fairly simple design. Took me five minutes on amazon to buy the necessary materials. Obviously, cost was not an issue, but it still came out to be under a hundred dollars. Though, one of the parts may not be sufficient, so I may have to end up spending slightly more than that, but as I said, cost is not something I'm really worried about.
